mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 exceeding 2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when this trigger is met (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 0.4 percentage points for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month + 0.4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in INDPRO below -0.5% for four consecutive months indicates a contraction in industrial production, reflecting weakening economic activity and reduced corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is in this regime (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in UNRATE and a fall in PAYEMS above 0.3% in the same month signals labor market tightness with stagnant employment growth, which increases cost pressures without expanding output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month + 0.3% AND PAYEMS < previous month - 0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during these joint events (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in HOUST above 2% from the previous month for two consecutive months signals a surge in housing demand, which typically correlates with broader economic expansion and supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month + 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive during these episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL below their respective 12-month averages signals a loosening monetary stance accompanied by falling inflation, which typically supports risk assets and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 12-mo avg AND CPIAUCSL < 12-mo avg in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both proxies fall below their 12-month averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in RSAFS above 5% from the previous month indicates a strong rebound in consumer savings, which can signal precautionary behavior and reduced consumption, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in the absence of offsetting fiscal stimulus.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS jumps by more than 5% month-over-month (t-test p > 0.10).
